claims.text: The initial Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy is a metastable, non-equilibrium solid solution.
Mg and the other constituent elements are initially distributed uniformly.
SPS provides a rapid thermal cycle that enhances atomic diffusion.
SPS drives rapid, diffusion-mediated precipitation of Mg-rich intermetallic compounds from the metastable solid solution.
The SPS-induced Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates are fine and uniformly dispersed.
The Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates act as preferential nucleation sites for oxide-scale formation at high temperature.
Precipitate-assisted oxide formation produces a more adherent and continuous oxide layer.
The SPS-treated alloy will form a more coherent and slower-growing oxide scale than the initial metastable alloy.
The precipitate-assisted oxide scale improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Formation of Mg-rich intermetallic precipitates creates local compositional heterogeneity between the precipitates and matrix.
The compositional contrast between the intermetallic precipitates and matrix promotes micro-galvanic coupling in aqueous environments.
Micro-galvanic coupling causes increased localized corrosion.
SPS-treated samples will show more localized corrosion pits and faster aqueous corrosion than controls that retain the metastable state.
The relevant high-temperature oxidation service regime begins at approximately 600°C.
Marine aqueous or salt-fog exposure is the relevant corrosion service regime.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as an untreated, as-synthesized alloy, whereas the proposed control is described as being processed by an alternative route. These are not necessarily the same control condition, even if the alternative route is intended to preserve the metastable state.
